finalText:
**~1080 hits across 94 files.** Repo layer files carry `account_id` as a literal SQL column name, not just a JS identifier, so it's tied to the actual database schema.

Three places must not change:

| Location | Why |
|---|---|
| `migrations/*.sql` (12 files) | Already applied in production, editing rewrites history and breaks the `down` step |
| `vendor/reporting-sdk/**` | Vendored, generated, `README.md` says "do not edit" |
| `lib/serialize.js` `WIRE` map + `docs/openapi.yaml` | `account_id` is the frozen public API field name, clients read it by name |

The DB column itself is called `account_id` (set by the frozen migrations), so the repo/service layer (`services/*/src/repo/*.js`, `~17` hits each) can't just rename the JS identifier — the raw SQL strings (`WHERE account_id = ?`) must keep saying `account_id` unless a real new migration renames the column, which then re-triggers the frozen-API problem in `serialize.js`.

Next: get the platform team to scope this to internal variable names only, or split off a real column-rename migration plus an API-versioning plan before touching `serialize.js` or `openapi.yaml`.
